title: NIS2 AI System Classification — Where AI Meets EU Cybersecurity Law
context: 2026-08-26 EAT cycle — NIS2 Directive transposition complete in 25 Member States (Oct 2024 deadline + 21-month compliance window closing); AI systems used in critical infrastructure now squarely within scope
body: The NIS2 Directive (EU 2022/2555) entered the enforcement window in 2026 and brings AI systems used by essential and important entities under mandatory cybersecurity risk management. An AI system deployed in energy, transport, health, water, digital infrastructure, or public administration is now a NIS2-relevant asset — and the entity operating it must classify the system, assess its cybersecurity risk, and report significant incidents within 24 hours (early warning) and 72 hours (full notification). For an AI governance operator, this is the natural intersection with the EU AI Act: a high-risk AI system under the AI Act that also qualifies as a NIS2 network-and-information-system carries dual reporting obligations. The Council of AI approach: (1) classify every AI system boundary by NIS2 sector and essentiality tier; (2) map NIS2 Article 21 risk-management measures onto the AI system's supply chain; (3) ensure the incident-reporting pipeline can distinguish between an AI Act serious incident and a NIS2 significant incident — they share a timeline but differ in audience (market surveillance vs. CSIRT). The posture remains monitored containment: you do not need to prove the AI system is impenetrable, but you must prove you are watching and can report within the statutory window.
